note: Set A reads specific, plausible values off the three polars and binds them to the right airfoil, Reynolds number and angle of attack (e.g. FFA-W3-211 peak cl/cd ≈120 at ≈7–8 deg, FFA-W3-360 ≈75, SNL-FFA-W3-500 cd ≈0.08 at cl = 1.5), with only one clear over-read (SNL cl = 2.0 at 20 deg) and two facts stated twice. Set B spends about a third of its claims on axis-limit 'ranges' and panel-title entities, and its 'increasing' trend claims are wrong because every cl/cd curve peaks at 7–10 deg inside the stated windows; several of its numbers (SNL cd 0.14, FFA-W3-211 cd 0.12 at cl ≈1.8, SNL cl 2.0) look like axis maxima rather than curve values. B does contribute a few good readings (FFA-W3-211 cl/cd ≈120, ≈−55 at AoA ≈−11 deg), but overall A is more correct, better conditioned and more useful.
remarks: The page is a pure plot page: the text layer contains only axis labels, tick numbers, legend entries and captions, so every numeric claim is a curve reading and every quote can only be a legend/axis label — quotes therefore never literally support the numbers in either set (flagged for both, not counted against either disproportionately). The text layer also drops the minus signs on negative tick values (e.g. '50 25 0 25 ...' for cl/cd). Both sets miss useful comparative facts visible in the figure: SNL-FFA-W3-500 (Re=8.1e6) has a far wider drag bucket (cd up to ≈0.10 over cl ≈−1 to 1.5) and a much lower peak cl/cd (≈25) than the FFA-W3 sections (≈75–120), and neither reports minimum-drag values. Note the page is filed under 'Blade Structural Properties' while the figure is aerodynamic polars — a heading/content mismatch in the source, not a fault of either extraction.
